mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reduces the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, leading to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as a persistent trend without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5.0% indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes corporate earnings weakness and triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.0% (or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer spending, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed their 3-month moving averages (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates sustained economic momentum and strong corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of late-cycle expansion periods when INDPRO is rising (or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) reflects a strengthening labor market, which supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as a persistent trend.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.0% indicates a restrictive monetary policy stance, which increases borrowing costs and dampens economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0% (or the Rank IC is positive over any 1-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of elevated federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 3.0%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 195) signals a monetary tightening cycle, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 3.0% and CPIAUCSL > 195 (or the Rank IC is positive over any 2-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: In an early-cycle expansion, accelerating GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates improving economic fundamentals, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of early-cycle expansion periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 1.0% (or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window).
